current.text: He is projected as Brooklyn's starting center after Nic Claxton was traded.
Brooklyn signed Mo Wagner. Wagner, Danny Wolf and Noah Clowney are bench big men who compete for center minutes.

His minutes are the open question. The experts expect about 24 minutes a night and say 30 is almost certainly not happening. The Wagner signing lowers his upside and may create a messy split at center.
He said he wants to double his minutes. In past Claxton absences he sometimes played very few minutes.
He is on a short two-year deal.
At about 24 minutes he projects as a top 100 category league player. At 27 to 28 minutes he would be about top 70. If he loses minutes, a pick near his Yahoo rank becomes a bad one.
He is Josh's best category league target. He is underpriced on ESPN, his Yahoo rank is about right for category leagues, and a Fantrax ADP near 101 is called free real estate.
In a mock auction he went for 10 USD as a starting center, which was still under the buyer's value.
Nine-cat rankings may make him look like a top 20 player, which he will not be.
Watch early in the season whether he actually starts. If he does not, react right away.

Brooklyn is projected to be one of the worst teams, at about 28 wins. Houston owns its pick, so it has no reason to tank. March minutes are uncertain because the team may shift minutes to young players such as Clowney and Minott.
Brooklyn has 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league. For a March 28 end its playoff schedule is 3-4-3, 10 games, with one back-to-back.
Yahoo lists him as questionable with a shoulder injury.

durable.text: He is one of the best offensive rebounders in the league by the numbers.
He is a strong per-minute producer who has rarely had the chance to start.
He used to be a shot blocker, but his blocks have dropped for unclear reasons. His passing and steals have gone up, and he has improved as a finisher and become a versatile defender.
His value is category specific: he rates clearly better in category leagues than in points leagues.

note: Sharpe is a cheap center target for us. Yahoo values him at 6 USD (average cost 4.0, rank 90) and ESPN has him near 0 USD, but one expert mock auction paid 10 USD and still called that under value. Projections have him at about 9 to 10 rebounds, 1.2 steals and a 54% FG% on modest volume, which fits builds that want boards, steals and FG% from the center spot, while his roughly 68% FT% and near-zero threes cost a little. Check right away whether he starts and gets 24 or more minutes ahead of Mo Wagner and Danny Wolf, and watch his shoulder (Yahoo Q). Note that Brooklyn has only 10 games in our playoff weeks.
